shared_rules.exam_design: Two original 100-point closed-resource forms, five 20-point domains. Suggested 300 minutes with nonprogrammable calculator, uncalibrated. Supply every needed numerical table and contractual assumption. Each form integrates all five volumes through linked economic reasoning; full prompt/solution point allocations and essential-domain thresholds. Explicitly list sampled outcomes and do not claim every detail of 60 chapters is tested.
shared_rules.mastery: At least 85/100 and 15/20 each domain plus unfamiliar transfer/teach-back; critical accounting, identification, units, funding, double-counting or integrity errors require remediation. Authored standards, not credential guarantees or calibrated equating.
shared_rules.financial_contracts: No unstated cash endowments, authority or whole-economy conservation. Date every collateral/settlement/claim cash flow; preserve unpaid nominal claims and differentiate economic writeoff. Say which resource/priority/funding policy is fixed. Exact original finite models preferred; chosen policy is only optimal under its stated finite decision rule.
shared_rules.code: Static fragments and standard-library Python only. Quiet check() returns strict JSON-safe summary. No author-checker expected-output self-comparison. Independent equations/oracles and focused economic interventions; purposeful small cases, not broad random grids. Run normal and optimized from another cwd; project CLI/API portable with documented bounded domain and non-destructive alias/input guards. Each author record binds nonself owned payload bytes/SHA256. Freeze before peer.
shared_rules.html: Fragments have no h1; root opening owns sole h1 for cumulative page. Exam anchors form-a/solutions-a and form-b/solutions-b; project anchor project. Every detail ID finance-core-a/b/project-prefixed. Scored li prompts have id and data-points; answers use data-solution-for. Links use actual flat reader filenames and anchors; planned successors link curriculum.html anchors.
shared_rules.evidence: Reuse actually inspected accepted primary-source scopes, accurately attributed; source record lists title/URL/canonical ID/exact scope. No new current legal/institutional claims without dated primary retrieval. Synthetic contracts do not require fabricated legal authority or market observations.
shared_rules.workflow: Send concise numerical architecture/blueprint before full prose. Root independently computes anchors and resolves design. Keep exact paths; no canonical/shared/deployment edits and no children. Root alone integrates and publishes after complete author, separate-peer and root gates.

assignments.scope: Original Form A built around an operating-company investment/acquisition and its investors or intermediary. Five connected but independently solvable 20-point cases. Combine reported accounts and working capital with incremental valuation; distinguish claim proceeds/ownership from face values; assess a funded portfolio or performance claim using physical and pricing data; derive a finite hedge and its actual collateral/settlement cash; close with a coherent downside/funding and governance recommendation. Avoid importing unstated outputs from earlier cases. At least one explicit all-recipient claim reconciliation and one boundary/global decision proof.

Original structurally distinct reassessment: prefer divestment/restructuring or a different production/ownership model, changed accounting estimates/information, constrained or liability-relative allocation, a different derivative or curve/credit mechanism, and a timing/authority change in a funded institutional decision. Five 20-point cases must require transfer, not merely new numbers from Form A. Include an independently derived feasible set/boundary, explicit retained claims and provider budget. Coordinate blueprint with root and Form A author before full prose.

Original integrated practical connecting actual operating transactions and claims to financing/valuation, a funded investor mandate, derivative/credit/settlement exposures, and an evidence-based institutional decision. Prefer one fictional operating group and a named outside investor/intermediary with two or three dated cutoffs and a small complete finite state law. Begin from original inputs, reconcile accrual income and cash, price appropriate claims with separately supplied positive state prices, distinguish physical risk weights, compare a finite menu of genuinely funded policies, trace collateral/creditor/ownership flows, and derive a meaningful reverse or sensitivity boundary. Include investment-policy objectives and implementation costs or constraints. Do not relabel Portlight, concatenate old chapter labs, or add broad simulation. Every external receipt must name payer/currency/date and stipulate funded scope; distinguish cash, economic value, book value and nominal surviving claims. Require independent learner analysis/code, decision memo and correction/evidence log. Six new transfer tasks with full answers; five-domain 100-point rubric and complete instructor benchmark.
